Formulation  
Occupational stress (precipitating) in a patient with busy teaching role (perpetuating) and limited described support. No prior mental health issues (predisposing minimal). Protective factors include employment and engagement with healthcare. Current presentation manifests as tiredness and dermatological symptoms potentially exacerbated by stress.

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Occupational stress  
- Patient Goal(s): Reduce stress levels; improve energy and coping at work  
- Clinical Goal(s): Assist patient to develop stress-management strategies and monitor for emerging anxiety or mood symptoms  
- Actions (Patient):  
  • Implement regular breaks and time management strategies at work  
  • Engage in relaxation activities outside work (e.g., exercise, hobbies)  
  • Monitor mood, sleep, and fatigue; seek review if worsening  
- Actions (Clinician/GP):  
  • Provide information on stress management techniques (e.g., mindfulness resources)  
  • Offer follow-up appointment in 2–4 weeks to review stress and overall wellbeing  
  • Consider referral to psychologist or EAP if stress persists or escalates  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Stress–skin interaction; basic stress-management options; when to seek further help  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased fatigue, mood changes, sleep disturbance, escalation of work-related distress  
- Coping Strategies: Scheduled breaks, relaxation exercises, social support, dermatological treatment adherence
